services.summary: A managed platform for deploying web applications as services, versions and instances in Standard or Flexible environments.
concepts: application, service, version, instance and traffic split form the core resource model for App Engine.
application source/configuration and inbound HTTP request enter the service; runtime sandbox/container, autoscaling and version routing govern processing.
managed web response and service-to-service call is the managed result, while dependent runtimes and data stores retain their own lifecycle.
applicationFit: Choose App Engine when the requirement centers on a managed platform for deploying web applications as services, versions and instances in Standard or Flexible environments.
It fits architectures where single application region, service/version boundary and VPC connector must be explicit and operationally owned.
Prefer Cloud Run for container-first serverless applications when that neighboring requirement is the dominant design constraint.

services.summary: A fully managed application platform for deploying stateless containers as request-driven services, event handlers, scheduled jobs, and finite batch workloads without operating servers or Kubernetes clusters.
concepts: A Cloud Run service exposes a stable HTTPS endpoint while every deployment creates an immutable revision containing the image and configuration.
Instances autoscale per revision from incoming requests, events or CPU utilization; minimum instances reduce startup latency and maximum instances protect cost and downstream systems.
Services handle requests, jobs run finite tasks to completion, and worker pools support continuous non-HTTP workloads; choose the resource type before tuning runtime settings.
applicationFit: Use Cloud Run for stateless APIs, web applications, webhooks, event consumers and containerized functions that fit the managed runtime contract.
Use Cloud Run jobs for migrations, scheduled processing and parallel batch work that must finish rather than listen on an HTTP endpoint.
Choose GKE when Kubernetes APIs, operators, custom scheduling or deep cluster control are requirements; choose Compute Engine when the workload needs VM or operating-system control.

architectureFlows.title: Public API with managed data
architectureFlows.note: A regional Cloud Run service terminates managed HTTPS, runs stateless application code and keeps durable state in managed services.

architectureFlows.title: Event-driven processing
architectureFlows.note: Events are buffered outside the container so delivery, retries and back-pressure are independent of instance lifetime.

architectureFlows.title: Private service-to-service API
architectureFlows.note: Each service uses a dedicated identity; the caller presents a Google-signed ID token and the receiver authorizes the invoker role.

security: Separate deployer identity from runtime service identity. Grant the deployer Service Account User only where needed and give each runtime service account the minimum downstream permissions.

Control inbound reachability with ingress settings and IAM. Public reachability and unauthenticated invocation are separate decisions; private service calls should use ID tokens and Cloud Run Invoker.

Store secrets in Secret Manager, restrict Artifact Registry access, use Binary Authorization where provenance is required, and route private egress through Direct VPC egress or an appropriate connector.
operations: Deploy immutable image digests, test tagged revisions without production traffic, then use percentage traffic splitting for canaries and rapid rollback.
Tune concurrency, CPU, memory, request timeout, minimum instances and maximum instances together; also protect Cloud SQL connection pools and other downstream quotas.
Monitor request latency, error rate, container startup latency, instance count, billable instance time, logs and traces by revision so regressions can be tied to a deployment.
watchPoints: A maximum-instance setting applies per revision; during a traffic split, total service instances can exceed the limit configured on one revision.
The writable container filesystem is disposable. Durable state must be externalized, and startup code must tolerate instance replacement and scale-to-zero.
Request-based and instance-based billing have different CPU-allocation behavior; minimum instances, VPC connectors and dependent services can generate cost even when request volume is low.
cost: Primary Cloud Run charges follow allocated vCPU and memory time, requests, and the selected request-based or instance-based billing mode; usage is rounded to 100-millisecond increments.
Minimum instances reduce cold starts but establish baseline compute spend. Higher concurrency can improve resource sharing when the application is concurrency-safe.
Include outbound data transfer, Serverless VPC Access or VPC networking, Artifact Registry, Cloud Build, logging volume, Cloud SQL and other dependent-service charges.
alternatives: Cloud Run — managed stateless containers, HTTPS services, events and jobs with revision-based deployment.
Google Kubernetes Engine — Kubernetes control, operators, complex scheduling, sidecars and portable cluster APIs.
Compute Engine — VM, operating-system, custom networking or specialized host control.
App Engine — opinionated application platform with versions and language/runtime conventions.

comparisons.name: Cloud Run
comparisons.fit: Best fit for stateless containers, APIs, event handlers and jobs with minimal infrastructure ownership.

comparisons.name: Google Kubernetes Engine
comparisons.fit: Choose when Kubernetes primitives and cluster-level customization are part of the requirement.

comparisons.name: Compute Engine
comparisons.fit: Choose when the application requires VM lifecycle, OS access or specialized machine control.

memoryHooks: Service = stable endpoint; revision = immutable deployment snapshot. Traffic moves between revisions, not between mutable containers.
Invoker IAM controls who can call the service; the runtime service account controls what the running container can access.
Exam clue: fastest managed path for a stateless container with scale-to-zero and HTTPS usually points to Cloud Run.
